title: Top Juicers for Fresh Juice at Home (2026)
summary: The Nama J3 is Tom's Guide's top juicer and the Nama J2 is BestReviews' top pick, with the AMZCHEF ZM1902 for budget slow juicing and the Hamilton Beach Big Mouth for cheap, fast juice.
method: Picks come from Tom's Guide (juicer guide updated Apr 17, 2026, judged on yield, cleanup and range of produce) and BestReviews (updated Sep 2026). Both put a Nama cold press juicer first and both include the Hamilton Beach Big Mouth, a Breville centrifugal juicer and a citrus juicer.
assumptions: Prices change often, so we quote what each source showed and tell you to check the current price. Tom's Guide tested the Nama J3 and the Breville Juice Fountain Elite, while BestReviews picked the Nama J2 and Juice Fountain Plus, so those are different models from the same brands.

products.name: Nama J3
why: Tom's Guide calls it the best juicer it has tested. It handled carrot and ginger easily, made some of the creamiest nut milk it has tried, and its parts come out for easy rinsing with few grooves for fiber to hide in.
A smaller and more portable alternative to the J2, it offers two filter sizes for more or less fiber and a 15-year warranty.
specs: Cold press, 130W, 9.7 lb, 8.9 x 6.5 x 15.4 inches
Tom's Guide's price box showed $499; check the current price
cons: Needs tipping to get all the juice out
Smaller hopper needs topping up for big batches
products.best_for: People who will juice often and want one dependable machine
products.skip_if: You only juice occasionally or want to spend under $100
products.amazon_listing: Nama J3 - Compact cold press juicer - Hands-free - White | Designed for Smaller Kitchens -

products.name: Nama J2
why: BestReviews' Editors' Choice and best overall cold press juicer. The 70-ounce self-feeding hopper lets you load produce and walk away, and the auger runs at 50 rpm so there is little friction or heat.
BestReviews says it extracts so efficiently that pulp is often nearly dry. With attachments it can also make nut milk, grain milk, smoothies and soups, and it comes with a cleaning brush.
specs: BestReviews lists $599 at Amazon; check the current price
products.best_for: Daily juicers who want to load it and walk away
products.skip_if: You want a cheap or compact machine
products.amazon_listing: Nama J2 - Cold Press Juicer - Hands-Free - Black | Wide Mouth Hopper fits a whole recipe -

products.name: AMZCHEF Cold Press Juicer ZM1902
why: Tom's Guide's best budget juicer. It was surprised that this sub-$100 slow juicer holds its own, with decent juice, a very small counter footprint, easy four-part assembly and no trouble with high-pulp produce.
It does not match the Nama, and it hit 80 dB in testing, which is louder than some cold press juicers, but still manageable.
specs: Tom's Guide's price box showed $99.99, marked down to $76.49; check the current price
cons: Yields are not always as high as they could be
Plastic construction and no listed warranty
products.best_for: First-time slow juicers on a budget
products.skip_if: You want hands-free juicing or the best yield

products.name: Ninja NeverClog Cold Press Juicer (JC151)
why: BestReviews calls it a great everyday machine for people new to juicing, with a 24-ounce juice jug and a 36-ounce pulp container for family-size batches.
Two swappable filters let everyone choose how much pulp they want, and the dishwasher-safe parts and anti-drip lever keep cleanup tidy.
specs: Two filters, 24-oz juice jug, 36-oz pulp container
BestReviews lists $119.99 at Amazon; check the current price
cons: Narrow feed chute, so you need to peel and chop produce
products.best_for: Families new to cold press juicing
products.amazon_listing: Ninja NeverClog Cold Press Juicer, 24oz Jug, 36oz Pulp, Charcoal, JC151 | 150W high-torque

products.name: Hamilton Beach Big Mouth Juicer
why: BestReviews' best juicer under $100. The 3-inch chute fits a whole apple or several carrots without chopping, its 800W motor makes juice in minutes, and the 80-ounce pulp bin can handle up to 25 apples before emptying.
Tom's Guide agrees that it is very efficient for the price and makes a lot of good juice, but says it is below average with leafy greens and very loud.
specs: BestReviews lists $54.95 at Amazon; check the current price
pros: Little prep thanks to the wide chute
products.best_for: Beginners and apple, carrot and orange juicers on a budget
products.skip_if: You mainly want green juice or quiet operation

products.name: Breville Juice Fountain Plus
why: BestReviews' best centrifugal juicer, with an 850W motor that powers through carrots and celery and still handles spinach and citrus. A 3-inch chute takes small whole fruits and a froth separator keeps more juice in your glass.
Tom's Guide tested the Juice Fountain Elite and called it a rare centrifugal juicer that can tackle kale and carrots, though it is very loud and yields less than high-end masticating juicers.
specs: 3-inch feed chute, froth separator, safety interlock
BestReviews lists $149.94 at Amazon; check the current price
cons: Large and heavy for small kitchens
Loud (per Tom's Guide on the Elite)
products.best_for: People who want fast juice and do not mind noise
products.skip_if: You have little counter space or juice mostly greens

tips.title: How to choose
items: Tom's Guide says centrifugal juicers are faster, cheaper and noisier, while slow or cold press juicers are quieter, extract more and preserve fiber.
Tom's Guide says a masticating juicer is better for spinach, kale and celery, while centrifugal models blitz through hard apples and carrots.
BestReviews notes a wide chute cuts chopping, but a compact machine may fit your counter better.
Most cold press parts need hand rinsing. BestReviews advises washing or soaking right after use so pulp does not dry.

faq: What is the best juicer overall?
Tom's Guide picks the Nama J3 and BestReviews picks the Nama J2, both cold press juicers with a 15-year warranty.
What is the best cheap juicer?
Tom's Guide's budget pick is the AMZCHEF ZM1902 slow juicer, and BestReviews' best under $100 is the Hamilton Beach Big Mouth.
What is the best juicer for oranges and lemons?
Tom's Guide picks the KitchenAid Go Cordless Citrus Juicer, which made 28 oz of orange juice from 25 oranges in under 15 minutes, and BestReviews picks the Elite Gourmet citrus juicer.
Can a juicer make nut milk?
Tom's Guide says some pricier models like the Nama and Tribest can make nut milk or sorbet.
